beats_rho_strict_definition: Winner/rho upper paired 95% limits and every cell ratio < 1 in both instructions and native process wall, on confirmation and replay. beats_rho alone is the confirmation point estimate of rho/winner exceeding one.
lineage: round-0006 tiny (parity) -> round-0007 tiny2 (strict win) -> round-0008 tiny2 + per-target descent certificate (re-measured under the merged checker)
panel: single-target (one public target per cold job)

The strict win still holds on every cell. Challenger ld_ic (IC-only: orbit name from the longest zero run, plus the serialisation change) not promoted: 0.9221 of the incumbent instructions but native upper limit 1.0443 on confirmation (1.0199 point); ld_canon alone 0.9758 at selection, not provisional.

round_0014.what_changed: shared: the worker built as one optimisation unit (fat LTO, one codegen unit, dead sections dropped at link time), which removes a quarter of the executable text without changing a line of source or a byte of any report, plus a tests-only fix to the arena tests. Both arms got faster and rho slightly more so, as pre-registered, so the winner/rho ratios are slightly worse than round-0013's while beats_rho_strict still holds on every cell; the strict-win record stays with round-0013. Challenger lto_ic (orbit naming from the longest zero run plus the serialisation change) not promoted a fourth time: 0.9226 of the incumbent instructions but native upper limit 1.0163 on confirmation; lto_canon alone 0.9772 at selection with native upper limit 1.08.

round_0015.native_timing_protocol: blocking process reap with independent watchdog; complete cold process wall; posix_spawn child without a fork of the evaluator; caps by prlimit before job delivery
round_0015.what_changed: nothing shared: the baseline is the round-0014 winner source unchanged (its source manifest hash is identical), so the incumbent measures the same executable on fresh fixtures. The IC-only challenger scan_io (orbit name from the longest circular run of zeros, the block scan keeping only each rest's abscissa, and the report serialisation change) reached 0.9059 [0.8802, 0.9272] of the incumbent instructions, the largest IC-only step the campaign has measured, and was still not promoted: native upper limit 1.0073 on confirmation and 1.0105 on replay, exactly as the pre-registration predicted from the process floor. scan alone measured 0.9642 at selection with native upper limit 1.0119. Development also recorded two dropped changes: reduction by folding a sparse modulus is 22-47% worse than the byte tables, and dropping the bounds check on those tables is a wash.

The PANEL changed, for the first time since round 0006. tournament.py gained --cells and --holdout-cells (defaults reproduce the rounds 0006-0015 panel exactly) and this round ran eight confirmation cells instead of five, adding n23a1 (subgroup 4,196,903, twice the largest cell previously tested), n31a0 at the highest usable degree, and n29a1 as a second holdout. round_0018b.headline: beats_rho_strict=False; winner=incumbent; cells where the winner is at or above rho: {'instructions': {'n23a1': 1.0231222850821338}, 'native': {'n23a1': 1.0062830313848707, 'n29a1': 1.0093027306775213}}
round_0018b.native_timing_protocol: blocking process reap with independent watchdog; complete cold process wall; posix_spawn child without a fork of the evaluator; caps by prlimit before job delivery
round_0018b.what_changed: two disjoint levers, both found by measurement and each with its own arm. block lowers the scan block's clamp ceiling from 64 to 16: the rule's shape is unchanged and so is every cell whose own value is already at or below 16, which is why n13a0, n17a1, n19a0 and n29a1 are an A/A control carried inside a live arm. column makes a column the orbit representative itself rather than [h] of it -- the representative is already in the order-r subgroup, so the second cofactor multiplication scaled every column by a constant and the row and the descent carried a matching constant -- and declares column_convention: representative, which round18-oracle-convention.patch teaches the checker to read additively. both is the two together. The pair-table row rule was measured first and left alone: it sits at the measured optimum at seven of eight cells, n23a1 included.

strict_win_record_eight_cells_replicatio.reading: the same executable, the same eight-cell panel and gates, a different fixture draw; beats_rho_strict true in round 0017 and false in round 0018b

strict_win_record_note: Cross-round ratios carry fresh-fixture variation at least as large as the differences between the recent rounds, so the record is not a precise ranking. The round-0014 winner source, unchanged and with an identical source-manifest hash, measured winner/rho 0.7818 instructions and 0.9424 native in round-0014 and 0.7372 and 0.9246 in round-0015 -- the same executable, different fixtures. Round-0013 holds the record on the native metric (0.9098) and round-0015 shows the lowest instruction ratio (0.7372); neither dominates, and the record is left where it was rather than moved on a difference this measurement cannot separate from fixture draw. Round 0016 widened the panel to eight cells and beats_rho_strict came back FALSE: the winner loses to rho outright at n23a1 (instructions 1.0656) and at n29a1 (native 1.0905), and the panel-wide native upper limit is 1.0288. The same receipts restricted to the legacy five cells still pass strictly (native 0.9341, upper 0.9653, every cell below one), so every strict-win record above -- round 0013 included -- is scoped to that five-cell panel and must not be restated at family level. The record pointer is left at round-0013 because it names the best five-cell measurement, not because the claim survives a wider panel. Round 0017 is the first strict win on the eight-cell panel; strict_win_record (five cells) is left at round-0013 because five-cell and eight-cell ratios are not comparable, and strict_win_record_eight_cells names the eight-cell record separately. Round 0018b (scan-block ceiling and the representative column convention) does not hold beats_rho_strict on eight cells; cells at or above rho: {'instructions': {'n23a1': 1.0231222850821338}, 'native': {'n23a1': 1.0062830313848707, 'n29a1': 1.0093027306775213}}. Read that with round 0018b's main result, which is about the record rather than about the new arms: the incumbent in round 0018b is byte-identical to round 0017's promoted winner, and under a fresh seed (2026091818 against 2026091717) the same executable measures 0.7115 [0.6206, 0.8188] against rho with n23a1 at 1.0231, where round 0017 measured 0.6702 [0.6050, 0.7443] with n23a1 at 0.950. Instructions are deterministic, so that difference is the fixture draw alone. ROUND-0017'S EIGHT-CELL STRICT WIN THEREFORE DOES NOT REPLICATE UNDER A FRESH SEED, and n23a1 is where it breaks; round 0017's own RESULTS.md had already warned that 0.950 at n23a1 was not a stable per-cell number. strict_win_record_eight_cells is left naming round-0017 because that round's receipts say what they say and are immutable, but the record must be read as seed-dependent and not as a property of the executable or of the panel.
